blocks.text: This chapter marks the transfer from Elijah to Elisha. Elisha sees Elijah’s ascent, takes up Elijah’s mantle, crosses the Jordan as Elijah had done, and is recognized by the prophetic company as Elijah’s successor. The sequence presents Elisha’s public emergence in the role formerly associated with his master.

The final episode is ethically and theologically difficult: after Elisha’s curse, bears kill forty-two of those who mocked him. The Hebrew phrase often translated “young lads” does not require that they were very young children; it can describe youths. That uncertainty about their age, however, does not remove the difficulty raised by the severity of the outcome.

Elisha’s succession begins a book that will move through royal coups and Assyrian conquest, then Judah’s reforms, Babylonian destruction, and Jehoiachin’s life in exile. This opening transition introduces the prophetic figure whose ministry occupies the book’s early movement.
